secret_scan_findings.note: Inspected for location, rule and usage pattern only. No candidate value was printed, transmitted or recorded. Nothing was baselined, rotated or changed.
secret_scan_findings.assessment_basis: Structural, not cryptographic. gitleaks flags these on entropy alone and cannot distinguish a synthetic string from a real key. The judgement below rests on where each string lives and what the surrounding test does with it.

findings.evidence: Passed as authorization= and args={'token': ...} into line.emit(), after which the test reads the written timeline and asserts the value was redacted. The file's docstring records that three real customer email addresses once leaked through this path, which is why the test exists.
Passed as a header value into timeline.emit() inside a session explicitly named 'scrub'; the test then asserts the redaction marker count.
Module-level SECRET constant, injected via c._key = SECRET, and line 329 asserts SECRET is NOT present in the request body. The value exists precisely so the test can prove it does not leak.

findings.category: test fixture — inline client key injection
findings.evidence: client._key = <literal> immediately after constructing ScribeClient() in a test; the surrounding assertions are about transcription output, not credentials.
Module-level SECRET constant with the comment 'injected: the Keychain is never read in a test'; lines 101-102 assert SECRET is absent from both the request body and the URL.

secret_scan_findings.residual_risk: All five sit in tests/ and none appears in application code or configuration. The pattern is consistent throughout: the string exists so a negative assertion can prove it is not leaked. The one thing structure cannot rule out is that a synthetic-looking fixture was originally copied from a live ElevenLabs key. Only the owner knows that.
secret_scan_findings.action_taken: NONE. Not baselined, not rotated, not modified.
secret_scan_findings.recommended_owner_check: Confirm that no fixture string in these five locations was ever a real credential. If any was, it must be rotated at the provider — baselining it would record a live key as acceptable.
